optimize_concurrency.note: The handler gate allows 4 optimizations. Levels 1, 4, and 8 run four waves. Level 16 runs two waves. canceled_request.note: The request context is canceled after 30 ms. A completed plan means the handler finished despite cancellation. overloaded means the gate rejected it.

overload.note: Completed requests are HTTP 200 responses with a plan. HTTP 503 overloaded is deliberate gate rejection. HTTP 429 rate_limited is a different limiter.

membership_metadata.note: Seeded heads omit membership_count, so they keep the migration default of -1. BackfillBatch reconciles those heads from the authoritative event. pending_before is 0 until the reconcile cursor exists; backlog_before is the live unknown count. Twenty deleted heads and one unreadable event are marked inside this measurement. Deleted heads stay out of the eligible backlog. The unreadable event must become membership_count -2, which is not an empty configuration.

concurrent_membership_rebuild.note: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY uses the simple query protocol. write_wait_ms is one concurrent update of a single membership row.

populated_index_build.label: Indexes were created on this populated disposable schema. CREATE INDEX takes ShareLock. The membership index is then rebuilt with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY so a writer can be compared.

maintenance.proposed_minimal_correction: Add a leading index on each listed foreign-key column. Do not remove the winner, repair, or derivation-job checks, and do not ship the diagnostic queries that omit them.

statistics_refresh_skipped.error: relay intelligence statistics were refreshed recently

maintenance.suspected_root_cause: Foreign keys to events(id) have no leading index, so each deleted event can seq-scan those child tables inside the cascade triggers.

tie_repair_cursor_page.note: Separate from the successful page. repaired is the number of ties fixed on this page, not a blend with the previous call.

tie_repair_idle_check.note: Tie scan is skipped while the cursor is idle. The function still inspects deletion tombstones.

probes.budget_window_note: Each scenario starts by deleting relay_probe_attempts from the last 2 hours and all relay_probe_leases. Seeded history is 3 hours old and stays in place, outside the 1 hour budget window. The delete simulates a new hour so a successful-claim sample cannot exhaust the global cap before a later scenario.

completion_digest.algorithm: sha256 of the canonical completion JSON, including observation order after sorting
completion_digest.note: hash_wall_ms times resultDigest only, with no SQL. stored_hex_bytes is the digest commitProbeResult wrote for the public-write completion. Identical replay carries that digest. A same-status submission with a different observation does not.

probes.completion_path_note: public_write and search use publishProbe, which stamps the observation time and then calls commitProbeResult. Gift-wrap, retention, replay, same-status conflict, expiry, and concurrent completion call commitProbeResult directly. Neither path dials a relay. result_digest is the sha256 stored by that commit.

concurrent_completion.note: All eight submissions use one observation time and the same writes. One commit is authoritative. The other seven must match that digest.

expired_lease_reclaim.note: claim_relay_probe checks the recent-attempt cooldown before it replaces an expired lease. The successful reclaim ages that attempt by 30 seconds, which is outside the 1 second minimum used here, and sets the lease expiry in the past.
